Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that frames the evaluation sprint and lists the success criteria, exit gates, and a set of verification scenarios we propose to run during the two-week pilot. Quick summary up front:

- Evaluation window: 2 weeks (validation runs on week 1, reliability tests + mock production traffic on week 2)
- Primary success metrics: avg inference latency & 95th percentile latency, end-to-end accuracy on your labeled sample, and token cost per 1k predictions
- Hard exit gate: no greater than 1% incorrect PII redactions in the labeled sample set
- Acceptance test set: 25 prioritized prompts + 3 integration flows (web UI, API batch ingest, streaming session)

Attachments: 20270607-map-proposal-v1.pdf (MAP + timeline)

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Can you share a small representative labeled test set (100–500 records) we can use for accuracy checks?
2) Do you have an internal threshold for allowable hallucinations or would you like Redwood's recommended thresholds?
3) Is SOC2 evidence required for the procurement milestone during the evaluation, or can we proceed with an MSA placeholder and add SOC2 during Dedicated onboarding?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm test data availability and preferred SLO thresholds
- We schedule a 60-minute kick-off (I can do Thurs 6/10 morning PT)
- Ben will draft the verification scenarios workbook and Grace will propose SLA gates

If that reads OK, I’ll send an updated MAP with Luke’s (engineering) verification checklist embedded.

Thanks —

Attaching verif-test-cases.xlsx (draft) and pasting the high-level acceptance checks here so everyone has quick visibility:

High-level verification scenarios (draft):
1) Prompt accuracy: 25 canonical prompts run against the provided 300-record labeled set. Pass if overall accuracy >= 92% and F1 for key entities >= 0.88.
2) PII redaction: run synthetic PII cases (50 records). Fail if >1% redaction misses.
3) Streaming stability: simulate reconnects (5% of sessions) and ensure KV cache recovers within 2 subsequent prompts and does not regress accuracy by >2 points.
4) Batch throughput: target 1k tokens/sec for steady state; p95 latency <250ms and <500ms at 2k tokens/sec burst.
5) End-to-end integration: web UI smoke (10 end-to-end flows) with no functional regressions.

Pass/fail rules: each scenario marked Critical/High/Medium. Critical must pass to proceed to the procurement milestone.

I included test harness snippets and a sample JMeter (batch) configuration in the workbook. Will iterate after Grace's SLOs and Lauren's procurement notes.

— Ben
QA Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround and for committing the representative set. Summary of what we’ll run in the evaluation and the acceptance logic (so the MAP is actionable on day 1):

Evaluation summary:
- Week 1: validation on de-identified dataset (functional accuracy + PII checks)
- Week 2: resiliency + throughput tests (streaming reconnects and burst load)

Key acceptance gates (must pass all Critical items):
- Accuracy: overall accuracy >= 92% on your labeled sample; entity F1 >= 0.88
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 250ms at 1k tokens/sec steady-state; p95 < 500ms at 2k tokens/sec burst
- PII redaction: <= 1% misses on synthetic and labeled checks
- Stability: KV cache recovers after reconnects within 2 prompts with <=2 point accuracy delta

Procurement note: Lauren recommends we proceed with an MSA placeholder for the evaluation and require SOC2 Type II evidence prior to any production data ingest. For the evaluation we’ll accept your de-identified dataset.

Next steps:
1) Kick-off meeting Thurs 6/10 10am PT (calendar invite sent) — agenda: MAP walkthrough, verification workbook review, access to test data, and security checklist
2) We’ll upload the verification workbook and test harness to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C
3) HubSpot will be updated with the milestones (see deal BRIGHT-2027-47): https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If this summary matches your expectations, we’ll treat the attached verif-test-cases.xlsx as the canonical source of truth for acceptance tests during evaluation.

Look forward to the kick-off.
